person.name: Albert_Einstein
person.summary: Albert Einstein (1879–1955) was a German-born theoretical physicist whose work transformed modern understandings of space, time, matter, and energy. While working at the Swiss Patent Office he published his 1905 “Annus Mirabilis” papers, including special relativity and the mass–energy relation E=mc², and a key explanation of the photoelectric effect. He later developed the general theory of relativity, received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics, emigrated from Nazi Germany to the United States, and used his worldwide fame to advocate for peace, international cooperation, and nuclear arms control.

chapters.headline: Formative European Years
chapters.bridge_statement: Childhood and youth in Germany, Italy, and Switzerland shape Einstein’s personality, skepticism of authority, and scientific promise as he progresses from schoolboy to prospective physicist.

chapters.headline: Student To Patent Visionary
chapters.bridge_statement: Einstein’s Zurich studies, early struggles for employment, and Bern patent office period culminate in his annus mirabilis papers that revolutionize modern physics while he builds a young family.

chapters.headline: Berlin Theoretical Breakthroughs
involved_people: Members of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
chapters.bridge_statement: As a leading Berlin professor, Einstein develops general relativity, sees it triumphantly confirmed, and attains international fame capped by the Nobel Prize amid personal and political tensions in Europe.

chapters.headline: Exile In America
chapters.bridge_statement: Fleeing Nazism, Einstein settles in the United States, uses his authority to warn of nuclear dangers, and becomes a moral voice on global issues while continuing his scientific work in Princeton.

chapters.headline: Final Princeton Days
chapters.bridge_statement: In his last years in Princeton, Einstein remains intellectually active on unified field theories and public questions until his death, leaving a lasting scientific and cultural legacy.

events.title: Birth in Ulm
events.description: Albert Einstein is born in Ulm in the Kingdom of Württemberg to Hermann and Pauline Einstein, members of an assimilated middle-class German-Jewish family. Shortly after his birth the family will move to Munich, where his father and uncle work in the fledgling electrical industry.

images.caption: Ulm Sparrow statue in Einstein’s birthplace, Ulm, Germany

events.title: Begins studies at Luitpold-Gymnasium
events.description: Einstein enters the Luitpold-Gymnasium in Munich, receiving a rigorous classical education under the authoritarian [[Prussian education system|Prussian school model]]. Though often at odds with the discipline and rote learning, he excels in mathematics and physics, reads popular science works on his own, and continues violin studies that will remain a lifelong passion.

Prussian education system.explanation: A highly centralized, authoritarian schooling model developed in 18th–19th century Prussia, emphasizing discipline, obedience, and rote learning in state-run schools.

events.title: Passes Swiss Matura in Aarau
events.description: After leaving the Munich gymnasium and joining his family in Italy, Einstein moves alone to Aarau in Switzerland to complete his secondary schooling at the liberal Aargau Cantonal School. On 3 October 1896 he receives his [[Matura|Maturitätszeugnis]] with top marks in the sciences, an important step that allows him to enter higher education while formally separating from both German citizenship and organized religion.

Matura.explanation: The Matura (German: Maturitätsprüfung or Maturitätszeugnis) is a standardized secondary-school leaving examination and diploma in several European countries that qualifies holders for university admission.

events.title: Enrolls at Zurich Polytechnic
events.description: Einstein enrolls in the mathematics and physics teacher-training program at the [[Eidgenössisches Polytechnikum|Eidgenössisches Polytechnikum]] in Zurich (later ETH Zurich). There he studies under leading physicists and mathematicians, often skipping lectures he finds uninspiring while working intensively on theoretical problems with a small circle of friends, including his fellow student and future first wife Mileva Marić.

Eidgenössisches Polytechnikum.explanation: The Swiss Federal Polytechnic School in Zurich, founded in 1855 and later renamed ETH Zurich, a leading institution for science and engineering education and research.

events.title: Joins Swiss Patent Office in Bern
events.description: After struggling to secure an academic post following graduation, Einstein accepts a position as a technical expert at the Swiss Federal Patent Office in Bern. Examining patent applications for electrical and mechanical devices gives him financial stability and daily exposure to practical problems in electromagnetism, even as he pursues his own theoretical work in his spare time with the informal "Olympia Academy" discussion group.

images.caption: Albert Einstein as a German-born theoretical physicist

events.title: Marries Mileva Marić in Bern
events.description: Einstein marries his former [[ETH Zurich|ETH]] classmate Mileva Marić in a civil ceremony in Bern, against the initial wishes of his family. The couple soon establish a household in the Kramgasse, later known as the Einsteinhaus, where they will raise two sons while Einstein continues to work at the patent office and develop his revolutionary ideas.

images.caption: Albert Einstein and his first wife Mileva Marić

ETH Zurich.explanation: The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich, a leading science and engineering university where Albert Einstein and Mileva Marić studied together.

events.date_note: Spans several papers published between June and September 1905
events.title: Publishes Annus Mirabilis papers
events.description: While still a patent clerk in Bern, Einstein publishes a series of four landmark papers in a German physics journal that together reshape modern physics. They explain Brownian motion, introduce the light quantum to account for the photoelectric effect, formulate the special theory of relativity, and derive the mass–energy relation E=mc², bringing him to the attention of leading physicists across Europe.

photoelectric_effect.explanation: The photoelectric effect is the emission of electrons from a material when it is illuminated by light, revealing the particle-like behavior of light quanta.

events.title: Leaves patent office for Zurich professorship
events.description: Einstein resigns from the Swiss Patent Office after being appointed associate professor of theoretical physics at the University of Zurich. The move marks his full entry into the academic world and gives him more time and institutional support to further develop his work on relativity and statistical physics.

events.title: Moves to Berlin as leading professor
events.description: Einstein accepts a prestigious position in Berlin as a member of the [[Prussian Academy of Sciences|Prussian Academy of Sciences]] and professor at the University of Berlin, while also becoming director-designate of a new physics institute. The move places him at the center of German scientific life on the eve of World War I, even as his marriage to Mileva Marić deteriorates and his personal life becomes increasingly strained.

Prussian Academy of Sciences.explanation: A leading learned society in Berlin, founded in 1700, which served as one of the foremost scientific academies in Europe until its dissolution after World War II.

events.title: Presents general relativity field equations
events.description: After years of intense work in [[general theory of relativity|Berlin, Einstein presents the final form of the field equations of the general theory of relativity]] to the Prussian Academy of Sciences. The new theory describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy, supplanting Newtonian gravitation and providing a framework for understanding phenomena such as the precession of Mercury’s orbit.

general theory of relativity.explanation: A fundamental physical theory, finalized by Einstein in 1915, that describes gravity not as a force but as the geometric curvature of four‑dimensional spacetime produced by mass and energy.

events.date_note: Date the confirming eclipse results were announced to the Royal Society and Royal Astronomical Society
events.title: Relativity confirmed by eclipse observations
events.description: British astronomers announce in [[London|London]] that measurements of starlight during the May 1919 solar eclipse match the light-bending predicted by Einstein’s [[general relativity|general relativity]]. The dramatic confirmation is widely reported in the international press, instantly making Einstein a global scientific celebrity and a symbol of postwar intellectual cooperation between former enemies.

images.caption: Negative of the 1919 solar eclipse for relativity test

London.explanation: Capital city of the United Kingdom, which in 1919 was the political and scientific center where the British announcement of the eclipse results was made.

general relativity.explanation: Einstein’s 1915 theory of gravitation describing gravity as the curvature of spacetime, which predicts that light passing near a massive body like the Sun will be deflected.

events.date_note: Einstein received the 1921 Nobel Prize at the 1922 ceremony
events.title: Receives Nobel Prize in Physics
events.description: Einstein is awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics "for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect." The honor, based on his work in quantum theory rather than relativity, consolidates his standing in the scientific community and provides financial resources he had promised in part to his former wife Mileva Marić under their divorce agreement.
involved_people: Members of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

images.caption: Albert Einstein official 1921 Nobel Prize portrait

photoelectric_effect.explanation: The photoelectric effect is the process by which electrons are ejected from a material when it is exposed to light, a phenomenon whose explanation helped found quantum theory.

events.date_note: Arrives in the United States after deciding not to return to Nazi Germany
events.title: Emigrates from Germany to the United States
events.description: Following the Nazi rise to power and anti-Jewish measures in Germany, Einstein renounces his positions in Berlin and decides not to return from a trip abroad. He travels to the United States and accepts a permanent appointment at the newly founded Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where he will live and work for the rest of his life while speaking out against fascism and racial persecution.

images.caption: Aerial view of Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton

events.title: Signs Einstein–Szilard letter to Roosevelt
events.description: At the urging of fellow émigré physicists led by Leó Szilárd, Einstein signs a letter to U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt warning that Nazi Germany might be attempting to build atomic bombs and urging American attention to uranium research. The letter helps prompt the creation of U.S. advisory committees that eventually lead to the Manhattan Project, although Einstein himself will be excluded from direct work on the program.

images.caption: Einstein and Leó Szilárd reenact signing Roosevelt letter

events.title: Declines presidency of Israel
events.description: After the death of Chaim Weizmann, the government of Israel informally offers Einstein the largely ceremonial post of President of Israel in recognition of his moral authority and support for Zionism. He respectfully declines, explaining in a letter that he lacks both the natural aptitude and the experience to deal with people and official duties on such a scale, while reaffirming his deep connection to the Jewish people and the new state.

events.title: Dies in Princeton
events.description: Einstein dies in [[Princeton|Princeton, New Jersey]], after suffering an aortic aneurysm, remaining mentally active and working on unified field theories until his final days. In accordance with his wishes, he is cremated and his ashes scattered in an undisclosed location, while his brain is removed for scientific study, reflecting his lifelong dedication to understanding the nature of the physical world.

images.caption: Bust of Albert Einstein in Princeton, New Jersey

Princeton.explanation: A university town in New Jersey, United States, known for Princeton University and the Institute for Advanced Study, where Albert Einstein lived and worked in his later years.
